data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Temperature/Humidity Infrared Radiometer
record.description: The Nimbus 5 Temperature-Humidity Infrared Radiometer (THIR) was designed to detect emitted thermal radiation in both the 10.5- to 12.5-micrometer region (IR window) and the 6.5- to 7.0-micrometer region (water vapor). The window channel measured cloudtop temperatures during both day and night. The other channel operated primarily at night to map the water vapor distribution in the upper troposphere and stratosphere. Sensor data from these two channels were primarily used to support the other more sophisticated meteorological experiments on board Nimbus 5. The instrument consisted of a 12.7-cm Cassegrain system, a scanning mirror common to both channels, a beam splitter, filters, and two germanium-immersed thermistor bolometers. In contrast to TV, no image was formed within the radiometer. Incoming radiant energy was collected by a flat scanning mirror inclined at 45 deg to the optical axis. The mirror rotated at 48 rpm and scanned in a plane perpendicular to the spacecraft velocity. The energy was focused on a dichromatic beam splitter, which divided the energy spectrally and spatially into the two channels. Both channels of the THIR sensor transformed the received radiation into electric outputs (voltages), which were recorded on magnetic tape for subsequent playback to a ground acquisition station. For more detailed information, see Section 2 in "The Nimbus 5 User's Guide" (TRF B14758). The THIR world montages were presented in "The Nimbus 5 Data Catalog" (TRF B17697). Both documents are available from NSSDC. A similar experiment was flown on Nimbus 4, 6, and 7.
